title: What IF You Were 10x Faster?
format: Long-form 10m19s, 16:9 (source 854x480 @24fps at the 480p cap), category People & Blogs. Second-person ('you') narrated hypothetical with a single male TTS-like/clean VO, short voiced dialogue lines from side characters, music bed under everything. Visual style: low-poly 3D toon-shaded stickman world (black round heads with a cream rim-light outline, coloured hoodies, flat-shaded suburbs) intercut with flat 2D 'explainer cutaways' (white line-art stick figure on navy blue grid, yellow/orange accent, bold sans numerals). Ends as an origin story for a shared 'Project IF' superhero universe (cross-links to the channel's 100x Stronger / Fly / Read Minds / Webs episodes).

title_pattern.notes: Brand-stamped 'What IF' (capital IF = channel name IFOLOGY) makes every title a series entry. 'You' puts the viewer in the body; '10x' is a concrete, easily imagined multiplier (not infinite, so consequences feel calculable). Super-speed is a top-searched superpower (tags target 'what if you had super speed', 'what if you were the flash'). The title promises fun; the video delivers physics problems + an action rescue + a cliffhanger - title stays simple and lets the thumbnail carry the emotion.
variants_to_try: What If Your Reflexes Were 100x Faster?
What If You Could Stop Time for 10 Seconds?

thumbnail.composition: Mid-stride hero character (blue hoodie, black round head, smug half-lidded smile) running toward camera-right occupying the right 55% of frame, legs spread in an extreme diagonal lunge, giant foreground sneaker sole near bottom-right; a red sports car on the left third is being out-run, driven by a shocked stickman with a sweat-drop. Afterimage ghost copies of the runner trail behind him. Night city highway with speed lines and motion blur.
thumbnail.text: '10x' top-right (white, heavy rounded sans, black outline); 'TOO' (white) / 'SLOW.' (yellow) stacked bottom-left, huge, with a full stop for attitude. The text is a taunt aimed at the car (and the viewer), not a restatement of the title.
thumbnail.colours: Purple/indigo night background with warm orange street lights; saturated red car vs. saturated blue hoodie (complementary hot/cold split left vs right); yellow 'SLOW.' echoes the car headlights. Black character heads give max contrast.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: A human outpacing a sports car - the car is drawn smaller/behind, the runner huge and closer. Smug calm face vs. panicked driver face = emotional contrast. Holds a branded protein drink (Feastables) as a product-placement/meme wink.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Instant read of the premise without reading the title (human > car = super speed). The taunt 'TOO SLOW.' adds attitude and a mini-story. Note: the thumbnail is a polished 2D illustration in a different (richer, more 'cartoon poster') style than the 3D video - thumbnail is made separately and is more dramatic than any frame.
thumbnail.style_note: Thumbnail is NOT a frame grab; it is a dedicated illustration with afterimage trails, motion blur and lens perspective. Our code-only thumbnails would need the same: hero in foreground lunge, beaten vehicle/object behind, 2-word taunt.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: You wake up late. School starts in 1 minute. You grab your bag, step out the front door, and you're sitting at your desk...
hook.verbatim_0_13s: You wake up late. School starts in 1 minute. You grab your bag, step out the front door, and you're sitting at your desk before the bell even rings. >> Did you just leave? >> I'm already here. So, what if you were 10 times faster?
hook.visual_0_5s: Close shot of the yellow-hoodie protagonist in a dark bedroom, eyes wide (0:00-0:03); cut to a low-poly suburban street with a blue car (0:04); cut to classroom with green chalkboard (0:06).
hook.device: Second-person relatable micro-scenario (late for school) solved instantly by the power - a 'show the payoff first' cold open in 8 seconds, then a comic two-line dialogue gag (mom on the phone: 'Did you just leave?' / 'I'm already here.'), then the title question as a stated thesis at 0:11 over an aerial title card 'WHAT IF YOU WERE 10X FASTER?'.
hook.notes: The hook is pure wish-fulfilment and relatable (everybody has been late). It also plants a seed at 0:21-0:27: 'your brain, your eyes, your reflexes stay normal. Remember that. It matters later.' - an explicit open loop paid off at 4:28 ('Going fast is easy, stopping is the problem').

beats.summary: Late for school; you're at your desk before the bell. Phone gag with mom. Title question stated.

beats.beat_type: rules of the power + planted open loop
beats.summary: Title card over aerial suburb; legs 10x faster but brain/eyes/reflexes normal - 'Remember that. It matters later.'
25 km/h sprint becomes 250 km/h: faster than highway cars and race cars; Usain Bolt 44 km/h; 100 m in under 1.5 s vs 9.58 s world record.
Track trials: coach whistles, looks down, you're already at the finish holding his water bottle. 'Run that again.'
Treadmill study: limit is how fast feet can push, not how hard - ground contact ~1/10 s for elite sprinters vs 1/100 s for you ('sounds like a drum roll').
Never late, chores done in seconds, pizza delivery faster than the shop, Naruto-run joke, soccer gag (ball left at midfield), run 100 km to another city for lunch.

250 km/h wind ~ category-5 hurricane; drag grows with square of speed (10x faster = 100x harder); bugs hit like pebbles; fix: swim goggles + human-bullet lean. Aside: no sonic boom (sound barrier would need ~50x), 'just confused pigeons'.
Soles grind away at highway speed; four pairs a month - mom's complaint gag.
1 kcal/kg/km; 70 kg x 200 km = 14,000 kcal/day = a week of food daily; second and third breakfast, cereal boxes the size of a microwave. Mid-roll subscribe lower-third at ~4:24.

beats.beat_type: twist: the real problem is stopping (open loop paid off)
beats.summary: Tunnel vision at speed; 1/5 s reaction = 14 m travelled; dog near-miss (lucky jump); braking distance 300 m (three football fields); turning needs a 1 km wide curve; crash through hedge into inflatable pool ('any% route' joke).

Cheetah: claws as cleats, tail as rudder - 'speed is only half, the other half is grip'. Buy track spikes, lean like a motorcycle, friends map every corner in red. Rule stated: start slowing down before you need to.

Kid chases ball into street, distracted truck driver; you're 400 m away (6 s at full speed) but arriving at speed would kill him. You brake 300 m out - sparks, smoke - arrive at walking speed, lift him to the curb; truck flattens only the ball.
Melted spikes, shaking legs, mum crying; the viral clip is named 'The Slowest Rescue Ever Recorded' - 'that's the point'.

Woman in grey coat at the door; black van with the other IFOLOGY heroes (telekinetic in blue hoodie, flyer in orange goggles, mind-reader in headphones, beetle-armour inventor, super-strong red-cap). 'Project IF' - 'What we don't have is someone who can get there first.' Mum: 'Be home for dinner.'

Tablet flashes red; mind-reader can't read the villain; live highway cam: every car stopped and floating; one figure stares into camera. 'Six of you, one alert, and for the very first time, a villain...'
'What would you do first if you were 10 times faster? And who do you think the villain is?' Comment + subscribe, end card 'IFOLOGY - every story starts with IF'.

pacing.sampled_visual_change_s: ~2 (nearly every 2 s sample is a different framing; camera moves inside shots too)
pacing.explainer_cutaway_share: ~20% of runtime on 2D navy-blue line-art diagrams, never longer than ~16 s at a stretch, always followed by a 3D comedy payoff
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~20-35 s: new number/stat or gag every ~10 s, a scene/problem switch every 30-50 s; explicit open loop planted at 0:27 and paid at 4:28; problems counted aloud ('first', 'second', 'third') then 'none of that is the real problem' twist at 4:24 (43%); climax rescue 6:53-7:52 (67-76%); crossover/cliffhanger last 2 min.
pacing.notes: Fast, dense narration (185 wpm) with almost no silence; every claim gets a visual. Dialogue lines are 1-5 words and always punchlines. Mid-roll subscribe lower-third at ~4:24 right before the twist.

art_style: Low-poly 3D toon world (flat-shaded pastel suburbs, warm golden-hour or purple-night palettes, soft ambient occlusion). Characters: featureless black spheres for heads with a cream rim-light outline and minimal white eyes/mouth decals, thin black limbs, coloured hoodies as identity (yellow = protagonist, blue = telekinetic, orange goggles = flyer, purple + headphones = mind-reader, red cap = strongman). 2D cutaways: dark navy background with faint grid, white single-weight line art, yellow/orange highlight accents, bold geometric sans numerals. Recurring props: neon-green track spikes, blue swim goggles.
techniques_worth_copying: Payoff-first cold open: a 10 s relatable micro-scenario solved by the power, then state the title question.
Explicit open loop in the rules section ('Remember that. It matters later.') paid off at ~43% as the twist.
Counted problems ('The first one... The second... The third...') followed by 'none of that is the real problem' - escalation ladder with a reset.
Every number gets an anchor the viewer knows: highway car, race car, Usain Bolt, hurricane, football fields, a week of food.
Real-science credibility beats ('Scientists actually tested...', 'And this part is real.') sprinkled between jokes.
Alternate 3D story shots with flat 2D diagram cutaways for every calculation; each diagram is 4-16 s and ends in a 3D gag.
Joke rhythm: stat -> punchline line of dialogue (coach, mom, kid, friend) every ~15-20 s; gamer/meme references (any% route, Naruto run).
Turn the power's weakness into the climax: the hero wins by going SLOW ('The Slowest Rescue Ever Recorded') - ironic title-drop.

Shared-universe ending: recruit the hero into a team of the channel's other what-ifs, cliffhanger villain, two-part comment question (what would you do / who is the villain) to farm comments and binge.
Character colour coding (hoodie colour = power) makes a cast readable with featureless faces.
Mid-roll subscribe lower-third placed just before the twist, not at the start.
weaknesses_vs_outliers: Very little; the 3D production is expensive. Middle section (problems 2-3, ~3:34-4:24) is list-like and the cut rate dips to 12-13/min there - the lowest-retention risk zone. Thumbnail style differs from the in-video style.
code_only_remake_needs: A reusable stick character rig in SVG/Canvas: black circle head with rim-light stroke, eye/mouth decal swaps (shock, smug, sad, wince), hoodie torso colour prop, 2-bone limbs with run-cycle, lean, jump, brake-slide, carry poses.

Pseudo-3D or 2.5D environments: layered parallax suburbs (houses, trees, fences, road with lane dashes), track/stadium, kitchen, classroom, savanna; time-of-day palettes (golden hour, purple night) as theme tokens. Full low-poly 3D is out of scope for Remotion without three.js - a flat 2.5D parallax version with strong rim-light outlines is the realistic target (or @remotion/three for simple low-poly scenes).

Speed vocabulary: motion-blur streaks, afterimage ghost copies (opacity-stepped clones), speed lines, wind lines, debris/leaf particles, camera shake, whip-pan transitions, sparks/smoke particles for braking.

2D explainer kit (navy grid bg, white line stick figure, icon set: brain, eye, bolt, stopwatch pie, dog, car, plate+flame, paw), animated measurement bars ('14 METERS', '300 METERS'), speedometer gauge, vertical scale chart, stacking-items comparison, dotted-route map draw-on.
Number typography system: bold geometric sans numerals that count up (25 -> 250 KM/H), timer chips (0.014s), scoreboard dot-matrix style.

Overlay types: title card over aerial, binocular/tunnel-vision mask with blurred periphery, phone-screen insert showing a fake viral video, CCTV found-footage frame (REC/LIVE badge, timestamp, scanlines), subscribe lower-third, end card with question banners.
Dialogue: 2-4 extra TTS voices (mom, coach, kid, friend, mysterious woman) with short lines; narrator at ~185 wpm; music bed with ducking; whoosh/brake/impact SFX library.
Cast/universe bible so later episodes can cross over (colour-coded heroes) and a cliffhanger template.
Separate thumbnail kit: big foreground hero in diagonal lunge, beaten object behind, afterimages, two-word taunt in white/yellow with heavy outline, multiplier badge top-right.
